In the rainy season the boards absorb moisture and swell, and the gap takes up the change in shape so that the floor does not buckle. In the dry winter the boards shrink and the joints between them widen slightly, which is normal.
p3_legal_01: Last month the archive office took in 140 newly registered files and completed their scanning and numbering, although 3 files with missing pages were held back from filing and will be registered once the material is complete. Over the same period it handled 86 requests to consult property records, 61 of them made in person and the other 25 through authorized agents.
p3_legal_02: An office lease contract records a term of 3 years, a monthly rent of 7800 yuan and a deposit equal to two months of rent. The contract provides for a three percent rent increase each year, with property management fees paid by the tenant, its main text has 14 clauses, and both parties signed on the last page and applied their official seals.
p3_legal_03: This equipment sales contract runs to six pages, stapled at the top left corner, with a page number printed at the bottom right of each page. A seal stamped across the page edges joins the sheets together, the last page holds the signature block, a red official seal sits beside the signature of each party, and the date line is filled in with blue ink giving the day the contract was signed.
p3_legal_04: The storeroom that holds the registration files has no windows and is kept at a constant temperature and humidity all year round, with more than twenty rows of silver gray mobile shelving inside. A number label is fixed to the side of each row, turning a handle makes the shelving slide left or right along its rails, and by the door stand a temperature and humidity recorder and, beside it, an entry and exit logbook.
p3_legal_05: The notarization of academic credentials begins when the party concerned hands the original diploma and an identity document to the notary office. The notary checks the originals and asks how the qualification was obtained, the notary office then sends a letter to the issuing school for verification, and once the school confirms the details, the notary issues the notarial certificate, the whole process taking about a week.
p3_legal_06: Before a batch of contract files enters the archive store, it goes through several sorting steps. The archivist arranges the contracts by signing date and stamps a page number on every page, and the catalog details are then entered in the registration ledger. Once the contracts are packed into archive boxes and each box spine is marked with the year and the first and last file numbers, the batch can be taken into the storeroom and shelved.
p3_legal_07: When renewing their supply contract, a small printing plant on the edge of town and its paper wholesaler shortened the delivery cycle from ten days to seven and added a clause on quality inspection. On the day the new contract was signed, the plant manager returned the original of the old contract to the archive room, and after registering it, an archivist placed it in a file bag and sealed it for storage.
p3_legal_08: Before taking part in an overseas trade fair, a small foreign trade company had its business license notarized at a notary office. The original license was examined and the articles of association were reviewed as well, three working days later a bilingual notarial certificate in Chinese and English reached the company, and the company then mailed it to the organizer together with the booth contract.
p3_legal_09: A complete written contract has three structural parts. The opening part states the title of the contract and basic information about both parties, the main body sets out the quantity and price of the subject matter as well as the performance period and liability for breach, and the closing part leaves space for signatures and seals, while some contracts also carry lists or drawings as attachments bound together with the main text.
p3_legal_10: By established archival practice, administrative records are kept either permanently or for a fixed period, and a fixed period is either 30 years or 10 years. When the period ends, an appraisal group reviews the records file by file, those still worth keeping stay in storage, those that have lost their value are destroyed only after registration and approval, and the list of destroyed records is itself filed and preserved.
p3_livestock_01: This week Henhouse 3 held 4200 laying hens, which produced an average of 3650 eggs a day. From Tuesday the feed was switched to a new formula, and by Thursday egg numbers had begun to rise again. About 3100 kilograms of feed were used over the week, the indoor temperature stayed between 20 and 23 degrees Celsius, and humidity changed little.
p3_livestock_06: At the weighing at the end of this month, the 28 finishing pigs in Pen 2 averaged 86 kilograms. Compared with last month, each pig gained 21 kilograms on average. Over the month the pen went through 1650 kilograms of feed, and water intake was about 8 liters per pig per day. Two of the pigs were on the light side and had been moved to a separate small pen.
p3_livestock_02: This ranch sits among low hills, and wooden fences divide the land around it into several pastures. The main office is a row of red brick bungalows, with two cylindrical silage towers standing beside it. The cattle shed opens to the south, and its roof is covered with light grey steel panels. A gravel road runs from the front gate to the door of the milking parlor, lined with neat rows of poplars.
p3_livestock_07: The duck farm is built beside a pond, and bamboo fencing divides the water into three sections. Several rows of low sheds stand on the bank, their floors covered with a thick layer of rice husks. Every morning, more than a thousand brown ducks pour out of the sheds onto the water, and the shallows by the pond are covered with their footprints. Sacks of corn and rice are piled behind the sheds.
p3_livestock_03: After the chicks hatch, keepers first move them into a prewarmed brooding room. For the first three days the room is kept at about 33 degrees Celsius, and the temperature is then lowered by 2 to 3 degrees each week. A little glucose is added to the drinking water at first, and the first feed is finely crumbled pellets. By the sixth week the flock no longer relies on extra heat and can be moved to an ordinary henhouse.
p3_livestock_08: Sheep shearing usually takes place in early summer. Workers first drive the sheep into a narrow chute and lead them one at a time onto a platform covered with canvas. Shearing starts at the belly and then moves along the flanks toward the back, so the fleece comes off almost in one piece. The shorn wool is then sorted by length and color, baled, and sent to the warehouse.
p3_livestock_04: Last Wednesday evening, strong wind tore a gap in the fence on the east side of the ranch. More than twenty sheep slipped out through it and scattered into a nearby alfalfa field. Two herders chased them on motorcycles for over an hour before driving the flock back into the pen. Early the next morning, the fence was fitted with new posts.
p3_livestock_09: Before dawn the day before yesterday, a Holstein cow gave birth to twin calves in the calving barn. By the time the staff on duty found them, both calves could already stand. One weighed 38 kilograms and the other 35, both a little lighter than ordinary calves. The farm set aside a small stall bedded with hay just for them.
p3_livestock_05: Dairy cows are ruminants, and their stomach has four parts. Feed first enters the rumen, where it slowly ferments with the help of microbes. While resting, a cow brings the cud back up into its mouth and chews it again, a process called rumination. An adult dairy cow usually spends seven to eight hours a day ruminating.
p3_livestock_10: Chickens have no sweat glands and shed heat mainly by breathing with their beaks open. When the air temperature rises above 30 degrees Celsius, their feed intake drops noticeably, and egg numbers fall with it. For this reason, henhouses in summer are usually fitted with fans and wet cooling pads, which carry heat away through evaporation and lower the indoor temperature by a few degrees.
p3_logistics_01: Early on Tuesday morning, the warehouse in the east of the city received 14 trucks and unloaded 2360 cartons. Household appliances made up three tenths of them, daily necessities four tenths, and food the rest. Outbound orders that day totaled 1875, which was 210 more than the day before, and the night shift worked 40 minutes of overtime as a result.
p3_logistics_02: One conveyor line at the parcel sorting center handled about 40000 parcels in 8 hours, an average of 83 per minute. Scanning failed on 96 parcels, and all of them were passed on for manual checking. Seven damaged items were logged, all with outer packaging crushed out of shape and contents intact, and they were resealed and sent out.
p3_logistics_03: This cold chain warehouse is divided into three temperature zones, and the buffer room at the entrance stays at about 10 degrees all year round. The floor of the innermost freezer zone is covered with nonslip steel plates, and dark blue plastic pallets are stacked along the walls. Fans near the ceiling run with a low hum, a row of heavy padded curtains hangs inside the door, and the curtains sway gently whenever a forklift passes through.
p3_logistics_04: The platform at the freight station is about two hundred meters long, with more than twenty loading bays along it. Above each bay hangs a number plate, and below it sits a steel dock plate that can be raised and lowered. The edge of the platform is lined with yellow and black warning strips, white parking lines are painted on the ground, and several trailers have backed up against the platform to wait for loading.
p3_logistics_05: After parcels enter the sorting center, they are first placed one by one onto a conveyor belt at the unloading bay. They then pass through a gantry scanner, where the waybill barcodes are read automatically. The sorting machine pushes each parcel into a chute according to its destination, and workers at the end of each chute load the parcels into the matching cage carts. Once full, the carts are pushed to the dispatch area to wait for the trunk line trucks.
p3_logistics_06: Before a batch of export goods is loaded into a container, the warehouse keeper first checks the carton count and the shipping marks. Next, forklifts arrange the pallets by weight from the back toward the door, with heavy goods on the bottom and light goods on top. Near the container doors, workers pack the gaps tight with wooden strips and air bags. Finally the doors are closed and sealed, and the seal number is recorded on the packing list.
p3_logistics_07: On Thursday evening last week, a truck carrying ceramic tiles was stopped by a height barrier as it entered the logistics park. The driver got out to look and found that the tarpaulin frame on top of the cargo box was above the height limit. The duty officer of the park guided the truck around to the north gate, where the passage had no height limit. The goods were unloaded before nine that night, and nothing was lost.
p3_logistics_08: During its month end stocktake, a warehouse found that two cartons of insulated cups held 12 fewer cups than the books showed. The warehouse keeper pulled up the camera footage and the signed delivery receipt from the day the goods arrived, and found that the cartons from the supplier had been one layer short from the start. After checking the matter, the supplier sent the missing cups within three days, and the books matched the stock again.
p3_logistics_09: The barcode on a shipping label corresponds to a unique waybill number, and each time the parcel is scanned at a stage, a record is left behind. Arranged in order of time, these records make up the tracking history of the parcel. If a scan is missed at some stage, a gap appears in the history, but the parcel is usually still moving through transit as normal.
p3_logistics_10: Truck freight is commonly charged in two ways, by weight or by volume. Light, bulky goods take up a lot of space but weigh little, so they are usually charged by converted volume. Heavy goods are compact and dense, so they are charged by actual weight. Carriers generally compare the results of the two methods and take the higher one as the basis for the freight charge.
p3_medical_01: On Monday morning, the internal medicine clinic of a community hospital saw 126 patients, about half of them on return visits. The registration office opened at half past seven, and by nine more than 80 numbers had been issued. Four doctors were on duty that day, each seeing more than 30 patients on average, and the clinic finished before noon.
p3_medical_02: The outpatient pharmacy filled 412 prescriptions that day, 37 more than the day before. The morning rush for collecting medicine came at around ten, with the longest wait at about 20 minutes. In the afternoon six windows were open at once, and the queues grew noticeably shorter. Before the end of the shift, the pharmacists restocked the medicines missing from the shelves.
p3_medical_03: The floor of the outpatient hall is laid with light gray tiles, and two rows of blue seats stand in the middle. The registration windows line up along the north wall, and an electronic screen above them scrolls the number of patients waiting for each department. In the northwest corner of the hall there is a water dispenser with a floor directory sign beside it, and a round clock hangs on the wall.
p3_medical_04: The height and weight scale of the health checkup center stands at the end of the corridor, with a square metal platform as its base and a bar that moves up and down on its upright post. A small screen on the front of the unit shows the reading once a measurement is finished. On the floor beside the device is a pair of yellow footprints, marking where the person being examined stands.
p3_medical_05: On the day of the checkup, each person being examined first collects a checkup form at the front desk on the first floor, then goes to the second floor to have blood taken. After the blood draw, a nurse measures height, weight and blood pressure, and a vision test follows. The last item is an electrocardiogram on the third floor, after which the form goes back to the front desk, and the report is issued a week later.
p3_medical_06: Once an electronic prescription reaches the pharmacy, a pharmacist checks the drug names and quantities, takes the medicines from the shelves and puts them into a sorting box. The box then goes to a second pharmacist for checking, and once it passes, it is labeled and sent to the dispensing window. When the number lights up on the calling screen, the patient collects the medicine at the window and signs for it.
p3_medical_07: At the start of this month, 186 employees of a factory came to the health checkup center in three groups for their annual checkup. The hospital had assigned 6 extra nurses in advance and opened two more windows in the blood collection area. The first group arrived at seven in the morning, and by noon the checks for all three groups were over, with nobody waiting longer than half an hour.
p3_medical_08: Someone left a cloth bag in the waiting area of the outpatient department, with an umbrella and a photo album inside. A cleaner found it and took it to the service desk, and the staff then announced it twice over the loudspeakers in the hall. Half an hour later, the owner came back to the desk, described what was in the bag, and collected it.
p3_medical_09: Outpatient appointments come in two types, regular and specialist, and regular ones can be obtained at the window on the same day, while specialist slots are usually released a week in advance. Each specialist slot comes with a fixed consultation time, and patients wait outside the consulting room at their assigned time. When all appointments for the day are taken, the hospital adds an extra regular clinic session in the afternoon.
p3_medical_10: Medicines in the pharmacy are stored in zones according to their storage conditions, with room temperature medicines on open shelves and refrigerated ones in a cabinet kept between 2 and 8 degrees. The cabinet temperature is recorded once in the morning and once in the evening, and the log sheet hangs beside the cabinet door. Medicines that look alike are never placed in neighboring slots, which reduces the chance of picking the wrong one.
p3_mood_01: An observation recorded the daily routines of twelve night shift workers over two weeks. They slept about six hours a day on average, and seven of them had a habit of napping in the afternoon. The seven who napped scored 7 on average on a mood scale, the other five averaged 5, and the scale had a maximum of 10. All the data were compiled by the shift leader every evening.
p3_mood_02: Twenty university students took part in a timed mental arithmetic test, with researchers monitoring their heart rate throughout. Before the test began, the average heart rate was 72 beats per minute, it rose to 88 by the fifth minute, and after ten minutes of sitting quietly at the end it fell back to 75. Most of them said afterward that the tensest moment came in the final minute of the countdown.
p3_mood_03: The rest room on the third floor of the office building is not large, with two light gray sofas side by side against the wall and a water dispenser in the corner. A few pots of pothos rest on the windowsill, and when the afternoon sun shines in, the room feels very quiet, so staff often come here to sit with their eyes closed for a quarter of an hour before going back to their desks.
p3_mood_04: An emotion board hangs by the door of the kindergarten classroom, with five round faces of different expressions drawn on it, arranged in order from laughing to crying. Each child has a magnet printed with a small animal, and when coming in each morning, the children stick their magnets under the face that matches their mood that day. Before school ends, the teacher notes down in a notebook how the magnets are spread across the board.
p3_mood_05: The stress test in the laboratory has three stages. In the first stage, participants sit quietly for five minutes while instruments record their baseline heart rate. In the second stage, they give an impromptu speech lasting three minutes in front of judges, and the third stage is ten minutes of relaxation with soft music playing, during which researchers watch how each measure comes back down.
p3_mood_06: Once it is past nine in the evening, the retired carpenter switches off the television and paces slowly on the balcony for a quarter of an hour. After pacing, he soaks his feet in warm water, leafs through a few pages of an old picture magazine, and lies down with the lights off before ten without fail. His family members say he has kept this bedtime routine for more than ten years and it is rarely disrupted.
p3_mood_07: Last Friday afternoon, a forklift in the warehouse suddenly stopped in the middle of the aisle, and several loaders had to switch to hand carts to move the goods. That evening, the team leader noticed that everyone was speaking much more quietly than usual and some sat on boxes staring blankly, and only after a mechanic fixed the forklift did the mood slowly lighten.
p3_mood_08: On the day the final exams ended, the study room of the library suddenly emptied by more than half, and the few students who stayed were no longer buried in their books but leaned back in their chairs talking about plans for the holiday. Toward evening, one student returned a big pile of borrowed reference books all at once, and the librarian saw him walk out the door with a much lighter step.
p3_mood_09: In teams with only a few members, moods often pass from one member to another. When one person keeps frowning and sighing, nearby colleagues are also more likely to seem gloomy within an hour or two, and conversely, when someone cheerfully tells a joke, the atmosphere in the room usually eases along with it. Psychology calls this phenomenon emotional contagion.
p3_mood_10: The workshop of this textile mill follows a fixed rest rule, under which workers leave their machines for a break of ten minutes after every two hours of continuous work, and most of them walk out into the yard to enjoy the sun. The workshop director has observed that since the rule took effect, operating errors in the afternoon have decreased and disputes among the workers have become less common than before.
p3_museum_01: Last month, the ceramics gallery of this museum received 4200 visits, and weekend visitors made up about sixty percent of them. The gallery displayed 38 celadon pieces, 29 of them intact and 9 restored. Staff recorded the temperature and humidity twice a day, and the room stayed at around 20 degrees.
p3_museum_02: A batch of newly acquired copper coins was weighed one by one during registration, totaling 1360 coins with a combined weight of about 5 kilograms. Of these, 1020 had clear inscriptions, 210 were heavily corroded, and the rest were fragments. The registration work lasted 6 days, and every coin received a separate number.
p3_museum_03: This lacquer box is round, about 24 centimeters across, and its lid fits tightly onto the body. The surface has a black lacquer ground with scrolling floral patterns painted in vermilion, and the lines are smooth and fine. The interior is coated with red lacquer, the rim is slightly worn, and a faint ring of craftsman marks remains on the base.
p3_museum_04: The textile hall on the east side of the museum is on the second floor, and the long, narrow gallery is dimly lit. Two rows of low glass cases line the walls, holding flat silk fragments and embroidered sleeves. At the far end stands a reconstructed wooden loom, and a panel beside it explains how warp and weft threads interlace.
p3_museum_05: Restoring a broken pottery jar usually proceeds in several stages. The restorer first cleans each fragment, removing surface soil and old glue. The pieces are then matched one by one by the shape of their broken edges and fixed with a reversible adhesive. Missing areas are filled with plaster, sanded smooth after drying, and finally tinted to match the aged surface.
p3_museum_06: Before an old painting is moved from storage to the gallery, a keeper checks its number against the condition photographs. The scroll is placed in a custom wooden crate padded with soft foam and paper that contains no acid. After arriving at the gallery, the crate rests for a day so the painting can adjust to the new temperature and humidity. The crate is opened and inspected the next day, and the painting goes up on the wall only after everything checks out.
p3_museum_07: Last spring, a farmer dug up an intact pottery pot while turning over a field and promptly reported it to the local cultural heritage office. When archaeologists arrived, they found three more ash pits and some potsherds nearby. After two months of cleaning, the finds went to the county museum, and the pot is now displayed in a Neolithic case.
p3_museum_08: Last week, the clock restoration team at the museum restarted a brass mantel clock that had been still for many years. Staff removed the rusted mainspring and fitted two new gears. Once it was running again, the clock kept within two minutes over three consecutive days. The museum then moved it back to the gallery, where it strikes the hour once a day at noon as a demonstration.
p3_museum_09: Textiles and paper artifacts are highly sensitive to light, and long exposure makes their fibers brittle and gradually fades their colors. For this reason, many museums keep the illumination on such objects at around 50 lux and rotate them on a regular schedule. After a few months on display, each piece returns to storage and rests in darkness for a while.
p3_museum_10: Bronze objects easily develop powdery corrosion in damp conditions, and this corrosion gradually spreads inward. To slow it down, storerooms generally keep the relative humidity below forty percent. Storage cabinets often hold desiccant, which is replaced regularly. Objects that already show corrosion spots receive local treatment first and are then returned to the cabinet.
p3_music_01: A community wind band held 22 rehearsals this quarter, with an average of 41 players at each one, and the trombone section had the most absences. The repertoire grew from nine pieces to fourteen, two of them folk songs arranged by the band conductor. The showcase concert at the end of the quarter sold 380 tickets, and the remaining seats went to students from nearby schools.
p3_music_02: Last month a piano tuner from a music store made 57 house calls, working on 49 upright pianos and 8 grand pianos. Each piano took about an hour and a half on average. Eleven pianos were pitched well below standard and took two visits to bring up to pitch, and another 4 had broken strings replaced.
p3_music_03: The seating in this concert hall is shaped like a horseshoe and rises in three tiers. The stalls are covered with dark red carpet, and a pipe organ stands behind the stage, its silver pipes arranged from short to tall in a fan. Dozens of curved acoustic reflectors hang from the ceiling, and the walls are lined with uneven wooden panels.
p3_music_04: The top of this cello is made of spruce, and the back and sides are of flamed maple. The body is about 75 centimeters long and coated with amber varnish. The neck ends in a head carved into a scroll, four strings run from the head down to the tail, and a metal endpin of adjustable length extends from the bottom.
p3_music_05: Before a symphony concert, the musicians arrive backstage an hour early to change into concert dress. Ten minutes before the start they take their seats on stage one by one. The concertmaster enters last and signals the oboe to sound the tuning note, and the whole orchestra tunes in turn. The conductor then walks onto the stage, bows to the audience and raises the baton.
p3_music_06: Recording a pop song in a studio usually takes several steps. The drummer and bassist first record the rhythm track, and guitar and keyboards are then layered on top. The singer records the lead vocal in sections, and the harmonies are recorded separately. Once all the tracks are done, a mixing engineer balances the levels and the stereo image, and mastering is the final step.
p3_music_07: Halfway through an open air concert last month, a rain shower began. The crew quickly covered the speakers beside the stage with tarps, and the band paused for about fifteen minutes while most of the audience stayed put. The show resumed after the rain stopped, all twelve planned songs were played, and as the crowd left, many raincoats were still dripping.
p3_music_08: A middle school choir won a gold award at a provincial competition. The group has 46 students, and its program was an unaccompanied folk song and a modern piece. Before the competition, the students rehearsed for half an hour every day during the lunch break. The girl singing the solo was steady in the high passages, and the judges specifically mentioned the balance between the voice parts.
p3_music_09: The pitch of a string instrument depends on the length, tension and thickness of the string. The shorter and tighter the string, the faster it vibrates and the higher the sound it makes. Pressing a finger on a string shortens the vibrating part, so the closer the finger is to the bridge, the higher the note.
p3_music_10: A staff records pitch on five parallel horizontal lines. The higher a note sits, the higher its pitch. A clef at the start of each row of music fixes the note names of the lines. The treble clef is mostly used for violin and flute, the bass clef mostly for cello and tuba, and the time signature shows how many beats each measure has.
p3_physics_01: In a simple pendulum experiment, students set the length of the pendulum to 1 meter and released the bob from a small angle. A stopwatch timed 30 complete swings in a row, and three trials gave 60 seconds, 61 seconds, and 60 seconds. The period worked out from these results was about 2 seconds, in good agreement with the theoretical value.
p3_physics_02: After a resistor was connected to the circuit, five pairs of voltmeter and ammeter readings were recorded. As the voltage was raised step by step from 2 volts to 10 volts, the current rose correspondingly from 20 milliamps to 100 milliamps. The ratio of voltage to current in every pair was close to 100 ohms, showing that the resistance stayed stable over the measured range. The room temperature stayed at 22 degrees throughout.
p3_physics_03: A vernier caliper consists of a main scale and a sliding vernier, and the smallest division on the main scale is 1 millimeter. The vernier carries 50 small divisions with a total length of 49 millimeters. One end of the caliper has a pair of jaws for gripping the outside of an object, and a thin rod extends from the other end to measure the depth of a hole.
p3_physics_04: This optics lab has no windows, and its walls and ceiling are painted matte black to reduce stray light. In the middle of the room stands a 1 ton optical table on vibration isolators, its top covered with threaded holes spaced 25 millimeters apart. Lasers, lenses, and mirrors are fixed to the tabletop, forming a winding light path.
p3_physics_05: To measure the specific heat of a metal block, a technician first weighs the block and the water in the calorimeter on a balance. The block is then heated in boiling water for ten minutes until it reaches about 100 degrees. It is quickly moved into the calorimeter, and the technician closes the lid and stirs gently. Once the water temperature settles, the technician reads the final temperature and calculates the specific heat from the balance of heat gained and lost.
p3_physics_06: When a piece of ice at minus 10 degrees is heated on a steady heat source, its temperature first rises to 0 degrees. The ice then starts to melt, and although it keeps absorbing heat, the temperature stays fixed at 0 degrees. After all the ice has turned to water, the temperature rises again, and at 100 degrees the water begins to boil, with the temperature once more holding steady.
p3_physics_07: Last Wednesday afternoon, the readings of a laser interferometer in the physics department suddenly began to fluctuate noticeably. After checking, technicians found that the fluctuations always coincided with vibrations from road construction outside the building. They fitted damping pads under the base of the instrument, and the next day the readings were steady again, with the fluctuations reduced to a tenth of their former size.
p3_physics_08: Last winter, a physics club at a secondary school went to an open field outside town to measure the speed of sound. Two members stood 660 meters apart, one struck an iron plate, and the other started a stopwatch on seeing the strike and stopped it on hearing the sound. The ten trials averaged close to 2 seconds, giving a speed of sound of about 330 meters per second, consistent with the low temperature that day.
p3_physics_09: When light passes at an angle from air into water, it slows down and bends toward the normal. That is why chopsticks standing in a glass of water look broken at the surface. Light leaving the submerged part refracts again at the surface, and when viewed back along the refracted rays, the chopsticks appear shallower than they really are.
p3_physics_10: Without air resistance, all objects fall with the same acceleration regardless of their mass. In a glass tube pumped down to a vacuum, a feather and a coin reach the bottom at the same moment. A feather normally falls slowly because air resistance is large compared with its weight. An object falling from rest drops about 5 meters in the first second.
p3_post_01: Last week the town post office accepted 312 ordinary letters, 47 registered letters and 86 parcels. Of the parcels, 29 were sent to other provinces, registered letters took two days on average from acceptance to signed delivery, the carriers went out twice a day, once in the morning and once in the afternoon, and no items were returned all week.
p3_post_02: The line maintenance crew covered 68 kilometers on inspection rounds this month, replacing 11 aging poles and tightening more than 230 loose line clamps. Of this, mountain sections made up nearly half of the workload, the inspectors walked about fifteen kilometers a day on average, and the total time the communication lines were down during the month was under three hours.
p3_post_03: This old post office was built in the 1950s, a red brick building of two floors with a dark green cylindrical mailbox standing at its door. In the service hall the wooden counter has been worn shiny, an old platform scale sits by the window, and behind the counter a whole wall is taken up by sorting racks, with the name of a village posted under each of the dozens of pigeonholes.
p3_post_04: The mailbag used by the carrier is made of dark green canvas, with a wide strap so that it can be worn across the shoulder. Three compartments are sewn inside, the front one for ordinary letters, the middle one for newspapers and the innermost one for registered letters and delivery receipts, and a faded serial number is printed on the inside of the flap.
p3_post_05: An ordinary letter goes through roughly five stages from being dropped into a mailbox to reaching the hands of the recipient. Every evening a postal worker opens the mailbox to collect the letters and takes them back to the post office to be postmarked, a sorter places the letters into different pigeonholes by address, early the next morning the letters travel by mail van to their destination, and a local carrier then delivers them to the door.
p3_post_06: When a break occurs in a communication line, the repair crew first uses an instrument to find the approximate position of the break, locates it along the line and climbs the pole, strips the two wire ends and joins them firmly, then wraps them tightly with waterproof tape. Colleagues at both ends then check the rejoined line with a line tester, and only once the signal is stable is the repair counted as finished.
p3_post_07: Last Wednesday, while delivering letters in the old town, a postal carrier found that the house number on one letter did not exist on that street. Instead of sending the letter back, he asked around at a small shop nearby and learned that the family of the addressee had moved to the next alley years ago, and that same afternoon the letter reached the hands of the addressee.
p3_post_08: Around New Year heavy snow fell day after day, two poles on the line to a mountain village were broken under the weight of the snow, and the landline phones in the village were cut off for two whole days. The line workers split into two groups and carried new poles up the mountain through the snow, at noon on the third day the phone service was restored, and the public phone at the general store at the village entrance began ringing right after.
p3_post_09: A postal code is made up of six digits, the first two standing for the province, the third for the postal zone, the fourth for the county or city, and the last two pointing to a specific delivery office. A sorter can tell the general destination of a letter from the code alone, and sorting speed has risen considerably as a result.
p3_post_10: When a registered letter is accepted, it is given a unique number, after which it is logged once at every stage, and on delivery the recipient signs to confirm. Ordinary letters have no such logging and are hard to trace once lost, whereas a registered letter can be traced by the number on its receipt.
p3_publicservice_01: The senior canteen in the Liuyin community serves two meat dishes and two vegetable dishes every day at noon, and over the past week an average of 118 people ate there each day, with 146 on the busiest day. Each lunch is priced at 15 yuan, residents aged 80 or over get 5 yuan off, and the canteen sold 826 lunches in total that week.
p3_publicservice_02: Yesterday morning the service hall issued 137 queue numbers in total, followed by another 98 in the afternoon, and each visitor waited 14 minutes on average. The social insurance window had the heaviest workload with 81 cases completed over the day, the tax window completed 47, and 5 other cases with incomplete documents were moved to appointments next week.
p3_publicservice_03: At the center of the small street corner park lies a round lawn, circled by a red rubber walking track, and wooden benches stand every few dozen meters along both sides of the track. A row of fitness equipment stands in the northeast corner of the park, a drinking water dispenser sits in the small pavilion next to it, and after dark the streetlights keep the whole lawn brightly lit.
p3_publicservice_04: The newly completed service hall is spacious and bright, with pale stone on the floor and a guidance desk facing the entrance. Eighteen general service windows line the left side of the hall, the right side is an area of automated service machines with printers and information kiosks, and the side along the windows has space set aside for a nursing room and a rest area.
p3_publicservice_05: Registering the vehicle and the apartment number at the property management front desk is the first step in getting a parking permit for an electric bike. Staff check the housing details and photograph the bike for the records, then print a numbered permit and stick it on the rear fender, and the vehicle details are finally entered in the ledger, all in less than ten minutes.
p3_publicservice_06: Adding an elevator to a residential block with six floors in an old residential complex went through five stages. Gathering the views of every household took a month, the design and the relocation of underground pipes took another month and a half, construction and installation lasted two months, and after completion the work went through quality testing and acceptance before the elevator officially entered service in September.
p3_publicservice_07: Last Saturday morning six long tables were set up in the square of a residential compound, where more than ten volunteers repaired electric fans and rice cookers for residents free of charge and also sharpened scissors. The event lasted more than three hours and fixed over seventy items of all kinds, and the few appliances that could not be repaired on the spot were registered, to be returned the following week.
p3_publicservice_08: Four public bicycle stations were added along both sides of an old street, each holding twenty bikes. In the first week after they opened, nearby residents borrowed bikes more than a thousand times, and based on the borrowing and return data, the operator added a temporary parking area at a subway entrance to ease the shortage of bikes during the morning and evening rush hours.
p3_publicservice_09: The first contact responsibility rule is used in many service halls. The staff member whom a resident asks first after entering the hall takes charge of guiding that resident all the way, so even when the matter is handled at another window, the same staff member takes the resident there and explains the documents the matter involves, and as a result wasted trips back and forth become much less common.
p3_publicservice_10: When visually impaired people walk along a sidewalk, they rely on the soles of their feet and a white cane to tell apart the textures on tactile paving tiles. Raised bars indicate that they can keep moving in that direction, while raised dots indicate a change in conditions ahead, and tiles of this kind are usually laid at crossings and in front of steps and also appear at turns.
p3_publishing_01: Last year a publishing house released 214 new titles, including 68 titles for children, 41 popular science titles and 55 literary works, with reference books and textbooks making up the rest. First printings totaled about 860 thousand copies, 17 titles were reprinted within the year, and the return rate fell by two percentage points from the year before.
p3_publishing_02: The production log of a printing plant for this week shows that three offset presses ran for 96 hours in total and finished five book titles, using about 42 tons of paper. On Tuesday the presses stopped for two hours to change the blankets. Of 300 finished copies checked at random, 4 had crooked binding, and all of them were pulled out for rework.
p3_publishing_03: This hardcover art book is nearly square. The cover is wrapped in dark blue cloth with the title stamped in gold at the center, and the spine is rounded. The inner pages are thick matte coated paper, 240 pages in all, each trimmed to a clean edge, and a beige silk ribbon marker lies between the pages.
p3_publishing_04: The binding workshop of the printing plant has a long production line. A gathering machine stacks the signatures in order, and a conveyor carries the book blocks to the perfect binder, where hot melt glue is applied to the spine. The covered books then pass into a three knife trimmer. In one corner of the workshop, finished copies wrapped in plastic film are stacked and waiting to be loaded onto trucks.
p3_publishing_05: A manuscript goes through roughly the following stages from submission to publication. An editor first reads the whole manuscript and suggests revisions, and after the author revises it, the text goes through three rounds of review and three rounds of proofreading. Typesetters complete the page layout, and proofreaders check for typos and punctuation errors. Once the cover design is final, the printer makes proofs, and the press run starts only after the sample copy is confirmed to be correct.
p3_publishing_06: An offset print run begins with platemaking. Prepress staff output the typeset pages onto aluminum plates, and once the plates are mounted on the press cylinders, the press operator adjusts the ink and water levels. A few dozen test sheets are printed first to compare the colors, and the full run begins when the colors pass. The large printed sheets are left to dry and then sent for folding.
p3_publishing_07: Just before a new book from a publishing house went on sale, an editor noticed that the price on the back cover had been printed wrong. Three thousand copies were already boxed. The editorial office contacted the printer the same day, and workers spent two days putting a new price sticker on every copy. Shipping was delayed by three days as a result, but the book still reached the shelves before the end of the month as planned.
p3_publishing_08: Last winter, a retired middle school teacher compiled old village photographs collected over many years into a book. The publisher organized three rounds of image selection for it, and 312 photographs were included in the end. The first printing of two thousand copies sold out within two months, and the local library also held a small exhibition for the book.
p3_publishing_09: Every formally published book has an International Standard Book Number. It consists of 13 digits that indicate, in order, a prefix, the country or language of publication, the publisher and the specific title. The last digit is a check digit calculated from the first 12, and it helps catch errors made during data entry.
p3_publishing_10: In book printing, several pages are usually laid out on one large sheet, which is folded to form a signature. Common signatures have 16 or 32 pages, so the total page count of a book is mostly a multiple of 16. If the main text falls short, blank pages or advertisement pages are added at the end during typesetting to fill the gap.
p3_retail_01: The community supermarket on the street corner took in nearly forty thousand yuan on the last Saturday of last month, with 1260 customer visits and an average spend of about 30 yuan per purchase. The best sellers that day were eggs and milk, with 420 boxes of eggs and 560 bottles of milk sold, and the frozen dumplings in the freezer sold out before evening.
p3_retail_02: At the inventory count at the end of the month, the stationery shop had 2150 items in its book inventory but counted 2138 on hand, a gap of 12 items concentrated in pens and erasers. The shop manager went through the delivery notes from the past week and found that 8 of them were free gifts left off the records, while the whereabouts of the other 4 are still being traced.
p3_retail_03: The shelving unit on the right of the entrance has five levels, with cases of bottled water on the top, cookies and chips in various flavors on the middle three, and large bags of rice and flour on the bottom. Price tags run along the edge of every shelf, ordinary goods carry white tags, and the tags on promotional items have been switched to a bright yellow.
p3_retail_04: Two rows of slanted wooden racks stand outside the fruit shop, with apples and oranges piled on them like small hills. The shop sits beside the entrance of the food market and covers only a little over ten square meters, a refrigerated cabinet against the wall holds watermelon and pineapple already cut and boxed, and a small blackboard above the checkout shows the prices of the day in chalk.
p3_retail_05: Yogurt spends one night between being unloaded and reaching the shelves. While unloading, the receiving clerk checks the quantity and production date case by case and signs for the goods only when everything is correct, after which the goods go straight into cold storage. Early the next morning, the stock clerk restocks on the principle that older stock goes out first, moving older batches to the front and placing newer ones at the back.
p3_retail_06: Preparations for the weekend promotion begin on Wednesday. The purchasing department picks the twenty products to be discounted, new price tags are printed on Thursday, and after closing on Friday evening the staff take down the old tags, put up the promotional ones and update the prices in the cash registers, so that by the time the doors open on Saturday morning, the promoted goods are already stacked in displays along the main aisle.
p3_retail_07: Eggs on special at only 9 yuan a box drew a long line outside a supermarket last Sunday before it had even opened. The three hundred boxes set aside sold out in under an hour, so the supermarket brought in another two hundred from its warehouse and put up a notice at the door stating a limit of one box per customer for the special.
p3_retail_08: At the checkout, a bottle of laundry detergent scanned at 5 yuan more than the price on the shelf tag, and the customer pointed this out on the spot. The cashier checked and confirmed that the tag had not been updated in time, then charged the price shown on the tag. Before closing that night, the store went through all of its price tags and found 7 more cases of the same problem.
p3_retail_09: In supermarkets, the shelf at eye level is the one shoppers notice most easily, so items that sell well are often placed there, which is where the term golden shelf comes from. Bulky or heavy goods mostly go on the bottom shelf, which makes them easier for shoppers to lift and also lowers the risk of the shelving tipping over.
p3_retail_10: A promotion offering the second item at half price is in effect the same as a 25 percent discount on two items bought together. Taking a shampoo priced at 20 yuan as an example, the first bottle costs 20 yuan and the second 10 yuan, making 30 yuan for the pair, or 15 yuan per bottle on average, while a customer who buys only one bottle still pays the full price.
p3_school_01: This term the eighth grade has 6 classes with 258 students in all, 134 of them boys. The midterm exam was held in week 10, and the average math score was 81, up 3 points from last term. The grade office also held two parent meetings that month, attended by more than 230 parents in total.
p3_school_02: The school library lent out 960 books in October, with history titles the most popular at about thirty percent of the total. The lunch break saw the most borrowing and returning, with an average of 90 visits a day. At the end of the month the librarians checked the shelves and found 12 books in the wrong places, all of which have been put back.
p3_school_03: The chemistry lab on the third floor has eight long tables with black tops, each with a sink fitted in the middle. Along the wall by the windows stands a row of fume hoods whose glass doors slide up and down. A periodic table hangs behind the lectern, and the iron cabinet beside it holds neat rows of beakers and test tubes, with a list of its contents on the door.
p3_school_04: The sports ground of the school lies south of the teaching building and is ringed by a red rubber track 400 meters to a lap. The track encircles a football pitch of artificial turf, with a white goal at each end. A concrete grandstand stands on the north side of the ground, and beneath it is a storeroom for sports equipment.
p3_school_05: Fifteen minutes before the exam begins, the invigilator brings the sealed bag of papers into the exam room and breaks the seal in front of everyone. Students fill in their exam numbers on the answer sheets and wait quietly for the starting bell. Once it rings they begin working, and when the final bell sounds they put down their pens and leave their seats, while the invigilator collects the answer sheets in seat order, counts them and seals them in a bag.
p3_school_06: From twenty past seven every morning, students stream in through the school gate, leave their bags in their classrooms and begin morning reading. At ten to eight the loudspeakers come on, and each class gathers on the sports ground for morning exercises. After the exercises the students return to their classrooms, the first lesson starts at a quarter past eight, and there is a ten minute break between lessons.
p3_school_07: Last Friday afternoon, students of Class 3 in the seventh grade were looking at onion skin cells in a biology lesson. The microscope lamp of one group suddenly went out, so its members took turns using the microscope of the neighboring group. After class, the lab technician fitted a new bulb and checked the remaining microscopes one by one, finding dust on the lenses of two of them.
p3_school_08: On the second day of the school sports meet, heavy rain fell from nine in the morning until noon, leaving a lot of water on the track. The referees moved the long jump and shot put events to the afternoon. After the rain stopped, several physical education teachers cleared the track with squeegees, the competition resumed at two in the afternoon, and every event was finished before evening.
p3_school_09: The timetable of this middle school is arranged week by week, with four lessons each morning and three each afternoon, each lasting 40 minutes. Chinese and mathematics have five lessons a week each, and physical education has three. When holidays shift the working days, the academic affairs office releases an adjusted timetable three days ahead and posts it on the notice board of every class.
p3_school_10: The final grade for a term combines coursework and exam scores, which count for thirty and seventy percent respectively. Coursework scores come from homework and class performance, and the subject teacher records them once a month. Students whose final grade falls below 60 can sit a makeup exam in the first week of the next term, and a pass on the makeup exam is recorded as 60.
p3_sports_01: A youth swimming hall in a city was open for 26 days this month and received 1,840 training visits in total. The morning training class averaged 35 swimmers a day, and the two weekend days were the busiest. The pool water was tested three times a day and kept at 27 degrees, and 12 lane dividers in the hall were also replaced.
p3_sports_02: At a county track and field meet, the winner of the 400 meter final for men finished in 52 seconds, and the best long jump among women measured 5 meters 36 centimeters. A total of 312 athletes took part over two days, three county records were broken, and on the afternoon of the second day the meet was paused for twenty minutes because of light rain.
p3_sports_03: The main floor of this gymnasium has room for two basketball courts, and its wooden boards are coated in pale yellow varnish. The stands around it have nine rows of seats for about two thousand people, and an electronic scoreboard is mounted at the highest point. At each end of the floor a door leads to a locker room, and skylights in the roof let in soft light during the day.
p3_sports_04: A standard table tennis paddle consists of a blade and two rubber sheets. The blade is usually pressed from several layers of wood, and the handle comes in two shapes, penhold and shakehand. A red sheet and a black sheet are glued to the two sides, each over a layer of sponge. The thicker the sponge, the more bounce the paddle gives when it strikes the ball.
p3_sports_05: A marathon runner usually prepares for a race over sixteen weeks. The first four weeks build a base with easy jogging, and the weekly distance rises step by step. The middle eight weeks add interval runs and long endurance runs. The last four weeks cut back the load, only easy runs remain in the final week, and in the three days before the race the runner eats more rice and noodles to store glycogen.
p3_sports_06: Before a volleyball match begins, the referee checks the net height and the pressure of the match ball. The two captains then choose sides, and the team that wins the serve starts the first set. A set goes to the first team to reach 25 points with a two point lead, and there is a three minute break between sets. If the match goes to a fifth set, the first team to reach 15 points with a two point lead wins.
p3_sports_07: An amateur football team came from behind to win a league match two to one on Sunday. The team conceded first in the first half, and at halftime the coach changed the formation and brought on two fast wingers. The team leveled the score in the seventieth minute, and in stoppage time a center back headed a corner kick into the goal, as family members in the stands rose to applaud.
p3_sports_08: The outdoor tennis courts at the city sports center were renovated last autumn. The work crew removed the cracked old surface, laid a new hard court in blue and green, and added lights for night play. On the first weekend after reopening, many people came to play, and all eight courts were booked from seven in the morning until nine at night.
p3_sports_09: Basketball has a shot clock. After gaining possession, a team has 24 seconds to attempt a shot, and the clock resets only after the ball touches the rim. If time runs out before a shot, a violation is called and possession goes to the other team. This rule speeds up the game and cuts down on stalling tactics.
p3_sports_10: High jump competitions raise the bar step by step. At each height an athlete has at most three attempts, and three failures in a row mean elimination. An athlete may choose to pass a height. If final heights are equal, the numbers of failures at that height are compared, and the athlete with fewer failures ranks higher.
p3_statistics_01: This questionnaire survey handed out 600 questionnaires in total and got back 542 valid ones, a valid response rate of about ninety percent. Among the respondents there were 271 men and 271 women, mostly aged between 25 and 40. The surveyors took three weeks to finish entering all the data, and the original forms are kept in a metal cabinet in the archive room.
p3_statistics_02: A clerk at a bakery counted the morning customers for seven days in a row. From Monday to Friday an average of 86 customers came each day, Saturday reached 132, and Sunday had 118. The seven days added up to 680 people, about 97 per day. The clerk posted these figures on the wall beside the cash register, making it easier for the owner to plan the stock.
p3_statistics_03: The archive room of the survey center is at the end of the corridor on the second floor, holding six rows of gray metal cabinets, with a year label on every drawer. On the long table by the window lie two calculators and a stack of blank questionnaires, and on the wall hangs a hand drawn bar chart marking the number of people in each age group, with colors running from light to dark.
p3_statistics_04: This wooden box used for sampling is about half a meter tall, painted dark green on the outside, with a small round opening on one side. It holds one hundred table tennis balls, each printed with a number from 1 to 100, and they make a crisp clinking sound when the box is shaken. A layer of soft cloth lines the bottom to reduce wear.
p3_statistics_05: This household sampling began with dividing up the area. The survey team split the households of the city into groups by street, drew two neighborhoods at random from each group, and then picked one household out of every ten by door number within each neighborhood. The questionnaires were delivered in person by surveyors, collected all together a week later, and checked twice after being entered into spreadsheets.
p3_statistics_06: Working out the class average is not complicated. The teacher first adds up the scores on thirty exam papers one by one to get a total of 2460 points, then divides the total by the number of students to get an average of 82. After that he separately counts how many students scored above the average, 17 in all, and this figure is noted on the last page of the grade book.
p3_statistics_07: On a market day in March, a survey team was conducting sample interviews at a township market and had planned to interview two hundred people, but heavy rain fell that day, the stalls closed early, and in the end only ninety or so people were interviewed. The team leader decided to come back on the next market day to make up the rest, and that day the weather was clear and the quota was soon filled.
p3_statistics_08: Last autumn, while sorting household water use data, a research institute found that the average water use of one neighborhood was about ten times that of the others. Staff went back to the site to check household by household, and it turned out that an extra zero had been typed during data entry, and after the correction the figure for that neighborhood returned to the normal range.
p3_statistics_09: An average is easily affected by extreme values. In a group of ten people, nine have commutes of about twenty minutes while the remaining one spends two hours each way, so the average for the whole group is pulled up noticeably. In such cases, statisticians often report the median as well, since it is closer to the actual situation of most people.
p3_statistics_10: The larger the sample, the smaller the sampling error usually is, but the two are not in a simple inverse proportion. When a sample grows from four hundred people to sixteen hundred, the error shrinks only by about half, because the error is inversely proportional to the square root of the sample size. For this reason, many large surveys keep their samples at one or two thousand people, since the gain from enlarging the sample further is quite limited.
p3_textile_01: This small garment factory received three orders this month, totaling 1800 shirts. The cutting room used about 2600 meters of white cotton cloth, keeping waste within four percent. The 12 workers of the sewing team worked in two shifts, each sewing an average of 25 shirts a day, and everything was packed into cartons before the end of the month.
p3_textile_02: A roll of linen leaving the mill measured 145 centimeters wide and 60 meters long, weighing about 180 grams per square meter. An inspector checked ten sample spots, finding slight color differences at two and a small broken yarn at one. Shrinkage was three percent along the warp and two percent along the weft, and the whole roll was rated first grade.
p3_textile_03: A dark gray wool coat hangs on the rack, reaching below the knee, with a wide notched lapel. Two rows of horn buttons are sewn on the front, three in each row, and a band of matching rib knit is stitched inside each cuff. The lining is burgundy twill silk, and the edges of the pockets are finished with a line of fine topstitching, so the coat feels thick and soft to the touch.
p3_textile_04: The second floor of the fabric market is lined with rows of long, narrow stalls, each with fabric samples hanging all over its front. The few shops near the stairs sell only cotton and linen, with bolts of cloth standing upright against the walls like a cluster of colorful posts. At the end of the corridor are stalls selling lace and embroidered trim, where samples in glass cases are displayed in sections by width, and a long wooden ruler lies on the counter.
p3_textile_05: When a tailor makes a skirt, the first step is to trace the outline of the paper pattern onto the fabric with tailor chalk, then cut along the lines to get the front and back pieces and a waistband. Next the edges are overlocked to stop fraying, and the two side seams are stitched together on the machine. After the zipper is fitted the waistband is sewn on, and finally the hem is rolled and pressed flat, and the skirt is done.
p3_textile_06: To make tie dyed cloth, the craftsman first folds white fabric according to the pattern and binds it tightly with cotton thread. The cloth is then dipped into a blue dye bath, lifted out and lowered again and again, so the color deepens layer by layer. The dyed cloth is rinsed many times in clean water, the threads are untied, and the cloth is hung on bamboo poles to dry, with white patterns left where it had been bound.
p3_textile_07: A tailor shop in the south of the city received an alteration order for a wedding gown, as the bride had found at her fitting that the waist was two centimeters too loose. The old tailor opened the side seams and took in the darts, then sewed the loose sequins on the skirt back on firmly one by one. The job had been scheduled for three days, and he finished it in two and a half, and on the day of collection the gown hung on a rack at the shop door, drawing many passersby to stop and look.
p3_textile_08: Last month, eight hundred sets of school uniforms ordered by a middle school were found before delivery to have sleeves that were short across the board. After tracing the cause, the garment factory confirmed that a stack of fabric on the cutting table had been stretched too tight during spreading, so the cut sleeve pieces shrank back by about one centimeter. The factory recut the sleeves for the batch, and delivery was pushed back by a week.
p3_textile_09: The warp yarns of a fabric run along the length of the bolt, and the weft yarns pass crosswise through them. Pieces cut along the warp hold their shape well, so pant legs and shirt fronts are mostly laid out along the warp. Pieces cut on the bias stretch the most and are often used for binding strips and skirts that drape heavily, but they are also the easiest to pull out of shape.
p3_textile_10: The surface of a wool fiber is covered with tiny scales, which hook into one another under hot water and repeated rubbing. As the fibers tangle ever more tightly, a sweater shrinks and stiffens, a process called felting. The care labels of wool garments mostly call for cold hand washing or dry cleaning, and after washing the garments are usually laid flat to dry so that the weight of the water does not stretch them.
p3_toys_01: In the stocktaking at the end of the year, the kindergarten toy room held 1280 wooden blocks stored in 16 bins, 32 jigsaw puzzles, 5 of them missing pieces, 47 stuffed toys and 19 clockwork cars, of which only 11 still ran properly. There were also 6 sets each of Chinese checkers and flight chess.
p3_toys_02: Eighteen middle school students came to the Saturday afternoon board game session and split into 4 tables. Over three hours they played 23 games in total. The shortest, a game of Chinese checkers, took only 9 minutes, while the longest, a word building game, lasted nearly an hour. When the game pieces were counted at the end of the session, 2 dice were found to be missing.
p3_toys_03: The tin frog on the counter is only the size of a matchbox, with green and yellow spots painted on its back. A set of small gears is hidden under its belly, and a brass key sticks out of its side. After the key is wound a few turns, the hind legs kick against the surface again and again, and the whole frog hops forward until the spring has fully run down.
p3_toys_04: The toy shop on the street corner has a narrow front. The left wall is lined with wooden cubbyholes holding spinning tops and marbles sorted by kind, and the glass case on the right displays all sorts of clockwork toys. Several paper kites hang from the ceiling. A low table stands by the window, and the block castle on it is left for visiting children to build on as they please.
p3_toys_05: A landscape jigsaw of a thousand pieces is usually begun at the border. Players first spread the pieces face up and pick out those with straight edges to form a ring. Then they sort the sky and the lake into several piles by color and assemble them block by block into patches of the picture. Pieces of similar color are the hardest to place and can only be matched one at a time by shape, so finishing the whole puzzle often takes several evenings.
p3_toys_06: Workers saw the body and wheels out of beech board following a template, which is the first step in making a wooden pull toy duck. After that, the edges are rounded off with sandpaper, nontoxic waterborne paint is brushed on and left to dry for a full day, the wheels are fitted onto the axles with wooden pegs, and a pull string is tied on. Before leaving the factory, each duck is also checked one by one to see that its wheels turn smoothly.
p3_toys_07: Last month, the community activity room held a block tower contest. The children taking part were split into six groups with a time limit of twenty minutes. The fourth group stacked long blocks crosswise in a grid pattern, and when the tower reached 130 centimeters it began to sway. The group members widened the base with small cubes and finally took first place with a height of 145 centimeters.
p3_toys_08: During the Spring Festival, a family dug out an old set of flight chess in the living room. When the box was opened, everyone found that one of the red pieces was missing. The little granddaughter fetched a red button from the sewing box to stand in for it, and three generations played around the board for a whole afternoon. In the end, that button was the first piece to fly into the finish.
p3_toys_09: A tumbler toy cannot be knocked over because its base is a hemisphere filled with heavy material, which keeps the center of gravity of the whole toy very low. Once the body is pushed to one side, the center of gravity is raised, and gravity at once pulls the toy back to its original position. It rocks back and forth a few times and then settles firmly upright again.
p3_toys_10: A Chinese checkers board is shaped like a star with six points. Each player starts with ten pieces in one corner, and the goal is to move all of them into the corner directly opposite. A piece may step into an adjacent empty space or jump over a single neighboring piece into the empty space behind it, and when the landing spots allow, it can make several jumps in a row in one turn.
p3_traffic_01: Bus Route 18 has 23 stops along its full length, and a single trip takes about 50 minutes. During the weekday morning peak a bus leaves every 6 minutes, and in off peak hours the interval grows to 12 minutes. Figures for last month show that the route carried nearly ten thousand passenger trips a day, with Friday evenings the busiest.
p3_traffic_02: On the first day of the long holiday, the railway station of the small city sent off 8200 passengers, the highest figure for a single day this year. The station opened 3 extra ticket windows and placed 40 volunteers in the square and the waiting rooms to guide travelers. The two extra trains added that day were both more than ninety percent full.
p3_traffic_03: The bus stop stands under a row of plane trees, with a curved translucent canopy and a stainless steel bench beneath it. The route sign is fixed at the east end of the platform and shows the first and last bus times of four routes. A yellow line is painted along the edge of the platform, and a row of raised tiles for blind pedestrians is set into the ground.
p3_traffic_04: In a second class carriage of the high speed train, each row has five seats, three to the left of the aisle and two to the right. The seats are covered in blue gray fabric, the backrests recline, and a folding tray table is fitted to the back of each seat in front. Above the doors at both ends of the carriage there is a screen that shows the train number and the name of the next station in turn.
p3_traffic_05: After arriving at the railway station, passengers first scan their identity cards at the entrance and pass through the security check, then look up their waiting area on the screens in the hall. Ticket checking begins a quarter of an hour before the train arrives, and passengers go through the gates onto the platform and find the boarding point for the carriage number on their tickets. Once the train has stopped, passengers board in turn and take the seats shown on their tickets.
p3_traffic_06: Night resurfacing on this stretch of road starts at ten in the evening, when the crew first sets out traffic cones at both ends and diverts vehicles into the opposite lane. A milling machine then strips away the old asphalt surface, with a sweeper close behind to clear the debris. After the paver has laid the new asphalt, a road roller passes back and forth several times, and by six the next morning the road is open to traffic again.
p3_traffic_07: Early on Tuesday morning, thick fog settled over the expressway on the edge of the city, and visibility dropped below one hundred meters. The toll station closed its entrance for a while, and vehicles already on the road drove slowly under the guidance of traffic police. The fog cleared at ten in the morning, the entrance opened again, and it was not until half past ten that all the vehicles held up at the toll station had passed through.
p3_traffic_08: This Monday, the Route 32 bus line linking the railway station with the new eastern district officially opened, with the first bus setting off from the station at six in the morning. On the opening day, the 12 electric buses on the route carried about 1500 passenger trips. Most passengers getting off at the terminus walked on to work in the nearby industrial park.
p3_traffic_09: Traffic lights at city intersections do not run on fixed timings, and many intersections adjust the length of the green phase to the volume of traffic. During the morning peak, the green phase for traffic heading into the city is longer, while the one for traffic heading out is shortened. Late at night, when traffic thins out, the lights at some intersections switch to a steady flashing amber.
p3_traffic_10: Metro fares in this city rise in bands with the distance travelled, at 3 yuan within 6 kilometers and 4 yuan for 6 to 12 kilometers, plus 1 yuan for every further 10 kilometers. Passengers tap their cards once on entering and once on leaving, and the gates work out the fare from the two stations. A trip that enters and leaves at the same station is charged the lowest fare.
p3_urban_01: According to the renovation plan for the old street in the eastern district, the street is about eight hundred meters long, its original road surface is nine meters wide, and after renovation it will be widened to fourteen meters, with a sidewalk three meters wide on each side. Along the street 46 new streetlights will be added and 120 ginkgo trees planted, and the work is expected to take five months.
p3_urban_02: The ledger of the landscaping station shows that the subdistrict completed three pocket parks last year, measuring 600, 850 and 1200 square meters, for a total of 2650 square meters. About nine hundred shrubs were planted in the parks, 32 benches were installed, and all the night lighting uses solar lamps.
p3_urban_03: The renovated neighborhood square is an irregular pentagon paved with light yellow permeable bricks, and in its center stands an aged pagoda tree, ringed by stone stools beneath it. On the north side of the square is a row of low flower beds, while on the south side an open space is left, where a few elderly people practice tai chi every evening.
p3_urban_04: The new bus shelter at the street corner has a roof of light blue steel panels with slightly upturned edges, and the whole shelter is about twelve meters long. Inside it is a row of stainless steel seats, a route map is posted on the glass wall behind them, and next to the map is an electronic screen showing how many minutes remain before the next bus arrives.
p3_urban_05: The renovation of this main road advances section by section. In the first two months, the construction crew closes the northern half, digs up the old surface and then replaces the storm pipes beneath it. In the third month the work moves to the southern half and proceeds the same way as in the north, and in the final two weeks asphalt is laid and lane markings are painted along the whole road, after which traffic resumes in both directions.
p3_urban_06: It took nearly a year for the community garden to turn from a patch of wasteland into what it is now. At first, the designer visited residents in the nearby buildings to gather their ideas about plants and seating. After the plan was finalized, volunteers cleared gravel and weeds in batches and loosened the soil, then planted Chinese roses and mint, and the garden officially opened in the spring of the following year.
p3_urban_07: After a rainstorm last summer, water at an intersection in the old town reached half a meter deep, and several cars stalled and stood in the water. A later inspection by the drainage department found that the pipe under the intersection was more than half blocked by tree roots, workers spent three days replacing that section of pipe, and since then the same amount of rain has not caused flooding again.
p3_urban_08: Last month, the riverside subdistrict turned a stretch of disused railway into a walking path, and on its first weekend open it drew large numbers of residents out for a stroll. Part of the original track was kept, set into the middle of the gravel path, many parents walked along the rails with their children counting the sleepers, and the caretaker estimated that visitors over those two days exceeded five thousand.
p3_urban_09: Generally speaking, the planning idea of small blocks with a dense road network is to divide large plots into smaller blocks, so that roads are spread evenly like a grid. In this way, traffic is dispersed over more roads, the distance pedestrians walk to a bus stop becomes shorter, and small shops along the streets tend to multiply as a result.
p3_urban_10: The surface of a city road is not perfectly level, as the middle is usually slightly higher than the two sides, forming a gentle curve called the crown. Rainwater that falls flows along the crown toward the roadside and then into the underground pipes through the drain inlets, so the road surface does not easily collect water. When a road is renovated, this slope is measured again.
p3_weather_01: On November 3, the rain gauge at the weather station in the north of the city collected 23 millimeters of precipitation between 8 in the morning and 8 in the evening, with more than half of it falling within two hours in the afternoon. The strongest gust of the day reached 14 meters per second at around 4 in the afternoon, and the average temperature was 6 degrees lower than the day before.
p3_weather_02: Last week the mountaintop observation post had a north wind on five days, mostly at force 4 to 6, and on Thursday night it briefly strengthened to force 8. Snowfall over the seven days totaled 11 centimeters, the deepest snow cover was about 9 centimeters, and the weekly average relative humidity was 72 percent. The temperature never rose above zero.
p3_weather_03: A thermometer screen is a wooden box painted white, with thin slats set at an angle on all four sides, so air can flow through freely while sunlight cannot get in. The box stands on a frame one and a half meters above the ground, and inside hang wet bulb and dry bulb thermometers along with maximum and minimum thermometers. Its door opens to the north.
p3_weather_04: The automatic weather station on the island stands in the middle of a flat patch of grass, enclosed by a wire fence about waist high. A wind mast ten meters tall rises from the center with wind cups and a wind vane at the top, a solar panel hangs halfway up the mast, and a gray data box sits at its base. A few steps away, a rain gauge is fixed on a concrete block.
p3_weather_05: At 8 every morning, the observer first opens the outer lid of the rain gauge, takes out the collecting bottle inside, pours the water into a dedicated measuring cup, reads the scale and enters the reading in the logbook. The observer then wipes the bottle dry, puts it back in place and finally closes the lid. The whole procedure takes about five minutes.
p3_weather_06: The life of a thundershower usually passes through three stages. At first the ground heats up and warm, moist air rises to form towering cumulus clouds. Next, water droplets and ice particles multiply quickly in the cloud, and heavy rain and lightning arrive together. Finally, sinking air takes over, the cloud gradually loosens, and the rain weakens until it stops.
p3_weather_07: One evening last summer, hail suddenly fell on a small town in the river valley. The largest pieces were as big as soybeans, and the shower lasted less than ten minutes. The seats of bicycles parked along the street were covered with white pellets. The weather station then sent staff into town to measure the diameter of the hailstones, and samples were packed in a cooler and taken back to the station.
p3_weather_08: After a strong wind in early December, technicians at the plateau station found that the anemometer was missing one of its cups and that the recorded curve had suddenly turned erratic at two in the morning. Three of them lowered the wind mast in the cold wind and fitted a complete spare set of cups. The data returned to normal in the afternoon, and the missing cup was later found in the snow more than a hundred meters away.
p3_weather_09: Under the meteorological classification, less than 10 millimeters of precipitation within 24 hours counts as light rain, 10 to 25 millimeters as moderate rain and 25 to 50 millimeters as heavy rain, while 50 millimeters or more is called a rainstorm. Snowfall is graded in a similar way, except that the thresholds are much smaller.
p3_weather_10: Wind direction refers to the direction the wind comes from, not the direction it blows toward. A wind blowing from the north is still called a north wind even though it pushes fallen leaves toward the south. For this reason the arrow of a wind vane always points to where the wind comes from, while the tail fin is pushed to the other side. Weather stations usually record wind direction using sixteen compass points.
